reason: Both correctly state the §412 3-month grace rule, that the window closed mid-April, that registering now won't unlock statutory damages or fees against this infringer, that registration is required before suing (§411), and that DMCA takedowns need no registration. A adds special handling cost, a speculative §1202 claim and the 5-year presumption. B adds the CCB route, which gives up to $7,500 per work without timely registration, and correctly notes its limits (US respondents only, 60-day opt-out). B's CCB point answers the literal question "can we still get statutory damages?" more completely. B is slightly better.
